in_DamageInventoryJSON.description: The damage inventory and the incident, on their own: {claimId, currency, incident{...}, damageInventory:[{ref,category,location,description,claimed,action}], totalClaimed}. Every item you assign has a ref - use it.

in_PolicyCoverageJSON.description: The coverage view of the policy: {policyId, currency, sections:[{code,name,limit,deductible}], sublimits:[{section,category,limit}], deductible, annualAggregate, namedPerils:[...]}. Everything your rules test about what the policy covers and to what limit. The policy's period, payment status and parties are screening's business and are deliberately absent. The exclusion, condition and endorsement WORDING is in in_PolicyClausesJSON.

in_PolicyClausesJSON.description: The policy's wording: {exclusions:[{heading,text}], conditions:[{name,text}], endorsements:[{name,text}]}. These are the sentences BR-16 requires you to quote.

in_CauseDetermination.description: The assessor's cause determination, as a plain sentence. This is what BR-15 compares the claim form's incident type against, and what governs the coverage reading where the two conflict.

in_EligibilityDecision.description: How eligibility screening resolved. Either a reviewer's decision, or the recorded fact that no human decided.

in_EligibilityNotes.description: The written reason screening resolved that way.

out_Findings.description: The finding envelope for this component. Every check this component owns appears in findings exactly once, whatever the result. No text value may contain a double-quote character.

component.description: The component that produced this envelope

step.description: The process step this component implements

conclusion.description: This component's one-word conclusion, from the closed list in the system prompt

findings.description: One entry per check this component owns, passes included

ruleId.description: The BR-nn rule this check implements

check.description: The check name, exactly as written in the system prompt

result.description: One of the results allowed for that check

flag.description: Whether this counts as a flag

escalationSubject.description: This component's own subject, or none

headline.description: One sentence a reviewer can act on, at most 140 characters

reason.description: Why this result, in the reviewer's own language

evidence.description: The exact words relied on, with the document each came from

quote.description: The words relied on. No double-quote characters.

cites.description: Rule ids used as evidence and not re-raised

context.description: Things a reader may want to know that are not findings

whyNotAFinding.description: Why it could not change what is paid, to whom, or whether the loss is covered

unreadable.description: Names of inputs that could not be read

out_Conclusion.description: This component's one-word conclusion, from the closed list in the system prompt. It is the same word as the envelope's conclusion field.

out_FlagSubjects.description: The comma-separated set of distinct escalationSubject values raised by this component that are not none, or the single word none when there are none. This component may only ever raise its own subject.

out_CoverageAssignmentsJSON.description: The machine-readable half of your answer, as JSON: {claimId, items:[{ref, section, verdict, ruleId}]}. One entry per damage item, using the ref it arrived with. verdict is exactly covered or excluded. section is Dwelling, Other Structures, Personal Property or Loss of Use. ruleId is the BR rule that decided it. This is what the settlement join reads - it never re-reads your prose to recover a verdict you already made. Every item in the inventory appears exactly once (BR-14). Budget 1200 characters. Emit STRICTLY VALID JSON - keys and string values wrapped in double quotes, exactly as JSON requires. The only prohibition is that no text VALUE may contain a double-quote character of its own.
